uncited: *   **Input:** A single high-resolution reference image $I_{512}$ rendered from a reference camera $P_{ref}$ (or real input image in inference, but synthetic in training).
*   **Output:** A predicted triplane $\hat{T}$ and associated rendered images ($I_f, \hat{I}_{128}, \hat{I}_{512}, \hat{I}_D$) from the encoder's triplane.
*   **Frozen Components:** EG3D generator (produces ground-truth triplanes $T$ and images), EG3D MLP decoder, EG3D super-resolution network, EG3D dual discriminator.
*   **Trainable Components:** Image-to-triplane encoder $E$, MLP decoder, super-resolution network, dual discriminator (fine-tuned).
*   **Trplane $T$:** A 3-channel feature map per plane (front, side, top) intersecting at the head center.
**Encode Reference View:** Render the reference image $I_{512}$ from camera $P_{ref}$ using $T$.
*   $L_{LPIPS}$: LPIPS perceptual loss [Zhang et al. 2018] between pairs $(I_{128}, \hat{I}_{128})$ and $(I_{512}, \hat{I}_{512})$.
The discriminator is fine-tuned to differentiate between images rendered from the encoder and images rendered from the frozen EG3D generator.
For human faces, this is the ArcFace identity loss [Deng et al. 2019a] with $\lambda_2 = 1$.
*   **Overfitting to Synthetic Data:** Naive optimization leads to models that perform well on synthetic data but fail on real images.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **When to Use:** When synthesizing 3D portraits from single images where multiview consistency is required.
*   **When Not to Use:** When real data supervision is preferred or when the target domain is significantly different from the EG3D training distribution.
It builds upon the EG3D architecture [Karras et al. 2020] and uses techniques from 2D GAN inversion [Richardson et al. 2021; Tov et al. 2021] for category-specific losses.
